Beams, crystals and target geometry

Describe an electron beam and a finite crystal, then run one small PXR/CBS simulation.

Choose a beam and crystal

An electron energy (keV) and a transverse FWHM (mm) describe the incident beam. The crystal has its own thickness (Å), transverse footprint (full widths in mm), and tilt (degrees). A crystal's lattice cut is distinct from its lab-frame tilt and from the reflections used in scoring. Material keys come from the catalog. Change "hopg" to another crystal key such as "silicon" to explore a different target.

Run one source calculation

Keep the physics and numerical settings separate from the beam and geometry. The sample histories below are a numerical estimator—not the number of electrons in a physical bunch. Bremsstrahlung is disabled to focus on the crystal's PXR/CBS source spectrum.

Interpret and experiment

The first plot is the configured entrance distribution; the second is the computed response-free source density. It is not a measured spectrum or detector count rate. The CrystalCut(beam_uvw=(0, 0, 2)) places a direct lattice _axis along the entrance-face normal; tilt_deg then rotates that face in the laboratory. Neither chooses which diffraction planes the radiation calculation sums. That is a separate numerical/reflection policy. Try changing one parameter at a time: first beam.energy_keV, then target.thickness_ang, then material. A different crystal may need a different cut or energy range. Only the finite sample is illustrated; do not use the curve quantitatively without convergence and validation checks. Compare the beam/target how-to, physics, and validation status.
